evaluationSemantics.criterionPassMeaning: The blind spot has an honest baseline, evidence plan, stopping rule, anti-gaming rule, and public-projection boundary. Passing does not mean the missing evidence has been recovered or the blind spot has been resolved.

knownLaunchTasksExcluded: Jamie approves the exact production commit
Dokku, domain, TLS, smoke, and rollback verification

controls.label: Human collaborator corroboration

baseline.interpretation: The public repository currently contains no governed first-hand collaborator note. Participant memory and AI-assisted archival review are not collaborator testimony.

currentEvidence: Source-backed records, public documents, repositories, and participant-memory leads
Explicit source-role and first-hand-witness boundaries
controls.gap: Material individual-role claims still need bounded corroboration from people who directly shared the work.
requiredEvidence: At least three permissioned collaborator notes across at least two project families
Each note identifies first-hand scope, uncertainty, collective context, and permitted public use
Contradictions and corrections remain visible rather than averaged away
passWhen: Three governed collaborator notes exist across two project families
Every note records permission and quote or paraphrase terms
No note is represented as independent evidence when it merely repeats Jamie's prompt
antiGaming: Never synthesize or backfill collaborator testimony
Never attribute an AI archival review to a human witness
Never count a request for corroboration as corroboration
controls.nextAction: Run a bounded corroboration sprint for NYC Artist Coalition, recent technical operations, and one Kansas City project.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Project collaborator evidence only after explicit use permission; preserve uncertainty and collective credit.

controls.label: Population denominator and archive completeness

baseline.interpretation: Several social surfaces have capture-date censuses, but owner exports and inaccessible historical surfaces remain open in multiple records.

currentEvidence: Capture-date population manifests for selected X and Facebook surfaces
Explicit recovered, not-recovered, duplicate, withheld, and owner-export-gap dispositions
controls.gap: A retrieved interface population is not necessarily a lifetime account population, and missing owner archives can change the denominator.
requiredEvidence: Every completeness claim names the surface, account, capture date, and denominator
Owner-export and platform-access gaps remain explicit
Not recovered remains distinct from did not exist
passWhen: Every population claim has a bounded denominator and capture method
Every unresolved owner-export or platform gap has an inquiry and stopping condition
No capture-date census is described as lifetime-complete without an owner export
antiGaming: Never convert not recovered into did not exist
Never call an interface result a lifetime population without a complete owner export
Never hide duplicate, withheld, or unavailable rows to improve completeness
controls.nextAction: Acquire and reconcile owner exports where available, beginning with the project accounts that currently have the widest stated gaps.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Publish only bounded counts with the surface and capture date close enough for a reader to understand the denominator.

controls.label: Collective credit and collaborator review

baseline.interpretation: The knowledge bank models individual, shared, collective, and institutional agency, but no formal collaborator review round is recorded.

currentEvidence: Agency graph with explicit credit scopes
Claim-level boundaries against sole authorship and sole causation
controls.gap: Structured credit rules do not substitute for the perspectives of collaborators whose work is represented.
requiredEvidence: A correction and dissent path available to represented collaborators
A bounded review note for at least two collective projects
Attribution changes logged without suppressing disagreement
passWhen: At least two collective project records receive collaborator review
Reviewers can correct, qualify, or dissent without granting Jamie veto power over their account
Public copy distinguishes Jamie's contribution from coalition and institutional outcomes
antiGaming: Never treat silence or non-response as approval
Never require a collaborator to endorse the portfolio's interpretation
Never collapse collective work into sole credit
controls.nextAction: Invite bounded review of the NYC Artist Coalition and KC Spaces Fund records with a plain-language correction and dissent option.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Use collaborator review to improve attribution, not to manufacture endorsement.

currentEvidence: Public-safe Harry J. Epstein modernization and stewardship claim

A 2026 source-backed team-memory proposal and method
controls.gap: The portfolio's strongest public civic history is deeper than its independently corroborated recent paid technical-operations record.
requiredEvidence: Recent examples covering requirements, tool choices, release or deployment, quality checks, and handoff
Independent or approved aggregate corroboration of scope and outcome
Clear separation between delivered client work, an operating method, and a proposal

Each example names Jamie's role, collaborators, delivery boundary, and observable result
Proposals and pilots are not labeled as completed client delivery
antiGaming: Never present a proposal as delivered work

controls.label: Outcome and impact evidence

Bounded delivery and participation outputs

requiredEvidence: Every public proof is classified as activity, output, outcome, or impact
Outcome and impact claims identify a source, time horizon, comparator where possible, and attribution boundary
Social engagement remains a distribution or response signal unless stronger evidence connects it to an outcome
passWhen: Every prominent proof names its evidence level
At least three portfolio projects have independently sourced outcome evidence
No activity or social metric is projected as impact
antiGaming: Never relabel output as outcome to improve the portfolio
Never use reactions, reposts, press volume, or attendance as impact by themselves
Never claim sole causal responsibility for a collective or institutional outcome
controls.nextAction: Classify current proof claims by evidence level and prioritize outcome-source research for recent operations, NYC Artist Coalition, and KC Town Hall.

controls.label: Role-specific positioning

currentEvidence: Role-fit language across work, resume, and technical-operations surfaces
LLM evaluations for positioning, evidence, voice, and reading burden
controls.gap: A broad interdisciplinary record can read as diffuse when each target role requires a different ordering of the same proof.
requiredEvidence: A role-to-proof map for all three target tracks
Role-specific page and resume variants that preserve the same canonical claims
Real-reader comprehension checks for role, level, and next-step fit
passWhen: Each role track has a ranked proof sequence and explicit exclusion rules
Unfamiliar readers can identify Jamie's target role and strongest matching evidence
Variants do not create unsupported or contradictory claims
antiGaming: Never change the underlying fact to fit a role
Never solve positioning by listing every project
Never treat an LLM's role classification as real-reader validation
controls.nextAction: Create the three role-to-proof maps, then test one application-specific composition from each map.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Reorder and compress governed proof for the role; do not rewrite canonical facts.

controls.label: Fresh-human hiring usability

baseline.interpretation: No governed usability record from an unfamiliar hiring reader is stored in the repository. LLM review is useful preflight evidence, not a substitute.

currentEvidence: Deterministic site checks
LLM evaluations for positioning, evidence, voice, and reading burden
controls.gap: The system does not yet know whether an unfamiliar recruiter or hiring manager can quickly understand Jamie's role, evidence, and intended next step.
requiredEvidence: At least five unfamiliar reviewers across at least two role families
At least three realistic tasks: identify role, find relevant proof, and decide or explain a next step
Time, success, confidence, misunderstanding, and correction data
passWhen: Five governed sessions are complete across two role families
At least four of five readers identify the intended role and one defensible supporting proof without coaching
Every material misunderstanding has a disposition or repair
antiGaming: Never count collaborators already familiar with the work as unfamiliar readers
Never coach a participant toward the intended answer
Never invent or simulate human usability results
controls.nextAction: Run five short task-based sessions using the staging site and the role-specific resume, preserving only consented aggregate findings.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Use aggregate findings to improve hierarchy and language; do not publish participant identities or raw session material.

controls.label: Job-search funnel learning

baseline.interpretation: The public repository contains no governed aggregate application-funnel baseline, and employer, contact, and application-level records must remain private.

currentEvidence: A portfolio and role-fit evaluation system
Private job-search working materials outside the public repository
controls.gap: Without aggregate funnel instrumentation, portfolio changes cannot be connected even cautiously to screens, interviews, referrals, or offers.
requiredEvidence: Private event-level tracking with date range, role family, application variant, referral, screen, interview, decision, and source
Public-repo storage limited to de-identified aggregate periods and methodology
Enough observations to distinguish signal from one-off outcomes
passWhen: At least one governed aggregate period exists with a declared denominator
Application variants can be compared without exposing employers, contacts, or private correspondence
No causal portfolio claim is made from a small uncontrolled sample
antiGaming: Never place raw application, employer, contact, or correspondence data in the public repo
Never cherry-pick only successful applications
Never claim the portfolio caused an outcome from observational funnel data
controls.nextAction: Define a private event schema and publish only a de-identified aggregate methodology plus a first bounded reporting period.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Keep the funnel private; only de-identified aggregate learning and methodology may enter the repository.

controls.label: External validity of the evaluation system

baseline.interpretation: Internal checks show consistency and resistance to known failure modes; they do not establish real hiring-reader understanding or job-search outcomes.

currentEvidence: Deterministic repository checks
Adversarial mutation tests
Fresh LLM holdout reviews
controls.gap: A system can optimize against its own judges while missing behaviors and interpretations that matter outside the system.
requiredEvidence: Real-human hiring usability results
Periodic blind review of claims and role fit by people who did not author the criteria
Comparison between internal eval predictions and later aggregate funnel observations
passWhen: At least two independent human review rounds are governed
Internal and external disagreements are recorded and used to revise criteria
The system reports calibration limits rather than declaring itself validated
antiGaming: Never treat deterministic or LLM eval success as hiring impact
Never label an internal agent run as a human judgment
Never discard external disagreement because it lowers a score
controls.nextAction: Pair the hiring-usability sessions with a blind claim-and-positioning review, then compare the external findings with current eval predictions.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Keep evaluation claims modest: the system controls evidence and composition risk; external human and outcome validation remains separate.

controls.label: Visual archive, rights, and evidentiary use

baseline.interpretation: The knowledge lifecycle includes a photo-feedback path and rejects self-interpreting images, but the large visual archive is not yet a governed public-ready corpus.

currentEvidence: Photo-feedback chain in the knowledge-bank lifecycle
Anti-gaming rule that a photograph is neither self-interpreting proof nor consent to publish
controls.gap: Images can strengthen specificity, reveal new research leads, or expose people and contexts without adequate rights, consent, provenance, or captioning.
requiredEvidence: Every selected image has rights, consent, provenance, caption, and evidentiary-function dispositions
Visual claims link back to governed sources or become research inquiries
Sensitive people, places, and documents receive explicit privacy review
passWhen: A pilot corpus for at least three priority projects passes all five dimensions
Every projected image has an accurate caption and use decision
Visual discoveries enter the claim lifecycle without becoming automatic proof
antiGaming: Never treat custody or presence in an archive as publication permission
Never treat an image as self-interpreting evidence
Never use visual drama to imply a role or outcome the record does not support
controls.nextAction: Run a three-project photo-editor pilot with rights, consent, provenance, caption, and evidentiary-function review.
controls.publicProjectionRule: Publish only images with an explicit use decision and captions that state what the image does and does not show.

requiredEvidence: Editorial review for motive, relationship, learning, and specificity
Dated or situated first-person material for any scene or remembered exchange
Clear distinction among fact, participant memory, interpretation, and public claim
passWhen: Every major case study includes a specific human stake without weakening source boundaries
Jamie confirms that the public composition sounds like him
No anecdote, quotation, motive, or emotional state is fabricated
antiGaming: Never fabricate an anecdote, quotation, motive, or emotional state
Never use generic inspiration language in place of a concrete stake
Never let proof jargon erase collaborators, conflict, uncertainty, or learning
